item.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
item.description: Hundreds of protests took place in cities across France. Most of them were peaceful but some turned chaotic and violent.

item.title: The state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal
item.description: NPR's Joel Rose talks with James B. Story, former U.S. Ambassador to Venezuela, about the state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal.

item.title: Scuffles and fires break out as protesters rally across France, joining students
item.description: Demonstrators across France converged with students Saturday to protest rising living costs, as the country's fiscal crisis deepens.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold
item.description: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.

item.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past
item.description:
More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past
are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.

item.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
item.description: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.

item.title: Israeli settlers beat Palestinians and a U.S. photojournalist in West Bank attacks
item.description: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians as they were harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday, injuring several people including a photojournalist working for The Washington Post.

item.title: Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating protests
item.description: Protests have intensified over a review of voter lists that critics say is politically motivated and threatens to disenfranchise voters. The Election Commission and Modi's administration deny these allegations.

item.title: Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in U.K. after support for pro-Palestinian group
item.description: The Irish author said her books can no longer be sold in the UK after she pledged the royalties to a banned pro-Palestinian group.
